problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Find a zero of a globally monotone, L-Lipschitz operator F:E→E. A zero x⋆ exists with ‖x0−x⋆‖≤R. No objective or potential representation is required.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Fresh stochastic operator evaluations g(x,ξ), with IID seeds, E[g(x,ξ)]=F(x), and E‖g(x,ξ)−F(x)‖²≤σ². Each evaluation counts as one oracle call; repeated access to a sampled operator is not supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform second-central-moment bound σ² at every query point, with unbiasedness and joint measurability. No samplewise smoothness or exponential-tail assumption is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Seeds are independent and identically distributed. All Params are public, including x0,L,R,σ,ε, with L>0, R≥0, σ≥0, ε>0; F and the sampling law are hidden admissible-instance data.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over oracle sampling and any algorithm randomness, under a fixed maximum oracle budget.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The output X must be measurable, its squared operator residual integrable, and E‖F(X)‖²≤ε². This is an operator residual, not necessarily a gradient norm.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Standard stochastic monotone Lipschitz root-finding with independent unbiased bounded-variance evaluations and an expected squared residual criterion.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Lipschitz Monotone Root Finding

We seek a zero of a monotone, L-Lipschitz operator F:E→E on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space E, where L>0. A given point x0∈E lies within distance R≥0 of a zero x⋆. At each query, the oracle returns an unbiased estimate of F(x) with mean squared error at most σ2, where σ≥0, using independent, identically distributed samples. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable squared residual satisfying E∥F(x¯)∥2≤ε2, where expectation includes oracle and independent algorithm randomness.

The root-finding problem is find x∈E such that F(x)=0. Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. Let Ω be the measurable sample space. The algorithm receives E, Ω, x0, L, R, σ, and ε; it accesses F through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity). For every x,y∈E, ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥0,∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Nearby zero). There exists x⋆∈E such that F(x⋆)=0,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic operator oracle). There exist a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under ν, the squared error ∥g(x,⋅)−F(x)∥2 is integrable, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=F(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−F(x)∥2]≤σ2. At call k≥0, a query x∈E receives the reply g(x,ξk). The measurable sample variables (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent with common law ν under a joint probability law on ΩN. Algorithm randomness is independent of this sample sequence.

Queries may be made at any point of E. Let P denote the joint law of the algorithm randomness and oracle samples. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its squared residual must be integrable under P, and EP[∥F(x¯)∥2]≤ε2.

comparisonHtml:
In a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel structure, F is monotone and globally L-Lipschitz, and F(x⋆)=0 with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. Here L,ε>0 and R,σ≥0. The jointly measurable oracle g has integrable values and squared errors, ∫g(x,ω)dp=F(x) and ∫∥g(x,ω)−F(x)∥2dp≤σ2. Samples are IID with marginal probability law p and joint law P. The target is ∫∥F(z(ξ))∥2dP(ξ)≤ε2. Result (1) constructs batched inertial regularized extragradient, tuned using L,R,σ,ε; the setup imposes no algorithm restriction.

Stochastic monotone root finding: StochasticLipschitzMonotone.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) InertialMonotoneResidual (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(1+LRε+σ2ε2ℓ2)
(2) RRSEG (Lee and Kim 2026), Cor. 6.2 O(1+LRε+σ2ε2log3⁡(2+LRε+σε)); A=0 specialization. (1) saves at least a factor ℓ when σ2ℓ2/ε2≥LR/ε; otherwise matches the deterministic order. (1) uses growing batches instead of two calls per update; does not cover composite inclusions.
(3) Accumulative regularization (Ji et al. 2026), Thm. 2.2 O(1+LRεh+σ2ε2ℓ3h2); 0<ε≤LR, unconstrained specialization. (1) replaces the statistical factor ℓ3h2 by ℓ2. For fixed L,R,σ>0, the total saving grows as ℓh2 as ε→0. (1) does not cover constrained variational inequalities.
(4) S-Dual-OHM (Yoon and Loizou 2026), Cor. 3.6 O((1+LRε)ℓ+σ2ε2ℓ2); samplewise monotone, uniformly L-Lipschitz maps; same-sample queries. (1) needs only mean regularity and fresh samples. On the overlap, removes the deterministic ℓ factor; total gain when σ2≲εLR/ℓ. Statistical order matches.

Abbr: ℓ=1+log⁡(1+LR/ε); h=1+log⁡ℓ. Costs count individual stochastic operator evaluations, including batches and inner solves; A denotes the additional maximally monotone operator in an inclusion 0∈F(x)+A(x).

Lee, Sucheol, and Donghwan Kim. 2026. Accelerated Algorithms for Stochastic Monotone Inclusions with Fixed Queries. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35631v1.
Yoon, TaeHo, and Nicolas Loizou. 2026. Dual-Anchor Acceleration Is Near-Optimal for Stochastic Monotone Root-Finding. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36033v1.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedMonotone

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticLipschitzMonotone

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  x0 : E
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.finiteE Params.completeE
  Params.measurableE Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → p.E
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q F O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k)
      (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    (∀ x y, 0 ≤ ⟪F x - F y, x - y⟫) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖F x - F y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, F xstar = 0 ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R) ∧
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedMonotone.IsStochasticOperator
      (p : Measure _) F g q.σ
  successful q F output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖F (output ω)‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖F (output ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticLipschitzMonotone
